## The change

Read these before touching code (all in your worktree unless absolute):
- `app/docs/architecture/estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` (the main note: the featured session as a mark, its rules, the home and admin screens), and the notes it links: `modelo-de-datos.md`, `invariantes.md`, `acceso-a-datos.md`, `tiempo-real-del-aula.md`, `novedades-por-mail.md`, `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md`, `feedback-de-sesion.md`.
- The program design: /home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/.scratch/preguntas-en-la-card/program-design/kurasu.md. Its eight branches and the Standards section name every type, function, component and file the change adds or touches, with the decisions Q1–Q3. Follow it. Where it and the notes disagree, the program design wins (its "Cambios a la fuente" section lists those points; the notes were already updated in `d09d518`).
- The design tree: /home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/.scratch/preguntas-en-la-card/design.md.
- The prototypes, which settle how the screens look and behave, not how they are coded: `app/docs/prototipos/inicio-responsive.html` (student home), `app/docs/prototipos/admin-sesion.html` (session admin: Destacada switch, enable modal, confirmations, Preguntas destacadas, Activar) and `app/docs/prototipos/admin-sesiones.html` (teacher session list).

Summary. Today the featured session is derived (the last enabled one). It becomes an explicit mark the teacher sets: `sessions.featured` and `sessions.featured_questions` (migration `0004_featured_session`, booleans default false, a partial unique index so at most one session is featured). `SessionSummary` and `SessionChange` gain `featured` and `featuredQuestions`. Only the featured session accepts student writes (voting on a poll, asking, voting and deleting a question, raising and lowering a hand): elsewhere they keep today's 404 (`PollNotFound`/`QuestionNotFound`/`SessionNotFound`), through one `featuredSession` check that replaces `visibleSession` in those writes. Activating a poll or turning on featured questions outside the featured session answers a new `NotFeatured` (409). Featuring a session that would stay disabled answers `SessionDisabled`. When a session stops being featured (because another one is featured, the mark is removed, or it is disabled), its active polls close, its raised hands are lowered and its featured questions turn off, all in one D1 batch with the session change: `Sessions.update` reads the leaving session's active poll ids, then runs `Batch.run([sessions.writes.update(leaving, {featured:false, featuredQuestions:false}), polls.writes.updateWhere(ids, {status: closed}) (omitted when empty), hands.writes.removeWhere({sessionId}), sessions.writes.update(id, change)])`; `Repository.writes` is the deferred version of the write methods (opaque `Write`), built in `repositoryOf` from the `statements` it already has; the new core port `Batch` (`core/src/batch.ts`) has the adapter `D1Batch` (`database/src/batch.ts`), wired in `worker.ts`. The leaving session's classroom gets `session`, `polls` and `hands` notices, and its changelog items are removed. Turning featured questions on creates the new changelog item `questions-opened`; turning them off removes it. The first vote on a poll no longer removes `poll-opened`. `GET /api/classroom` enters the marked session; with no featured session nobody enters. The announcement mail links the featured session to `/` and the others to `/?sesion=<id>` (unchanged), and names "Preguntas abiertas" when they are on.

Web: the student home shows the featured card (`HighlightedSession` → `FeaturedSession`) with active polls of the featured session only and, when featured questions are on, a questions panel (`FeaturedQuestions`: the three most voted plus the student's own, "Mostrar N preguntas más" / "Mostrar menos", reusing `QuestionForm`, `QuestionList` with `emptyText`, `VoteToggle`, `DeleteOwnQuestion`). The list below is always titled "Todas las sesiones" (`EarlierSessions` → `AllSessions`) and includes the featured one, whose node is a star on red; no node shows a number; the featured card in the list shows "Entrar al aula"; `?sesion=<id>` of the featured session opens its card in the list. `railLook` (done/live/later) in `rail-look.ts` is shared by home and admin; `icons.ts` adds "star" (26px in the 44px node, 20px in the 32px mobile node). `/aula` takes the featured session by the mark. Admin of a session: `FeaturedSwitch`, `EnableSessionDialog` (narrow `Sheet`, opened when enabling), confirmations through `ConfirmDialog` (new `content` slot and `confirmIcon`) with `FeaturedEffects` counting active polls and raised hands via `useAdminPolls`/`useAdminRaisedHands`; `ContentTab` gets the featured session once via `useFeaturedSession` (`useAdminSessions({...options, select: findFeatured})`, module-level select) and passes it to `EnabledSwitch` and `FeaturedSwitch`; dialogs name the other featured session by title; "Sesión N de M" goes away (hero and Contenido card); `useUpdateSession` applies no optimistic patch for the waiting changes and invalidates sessions, adminSessions, adminChangelog, allAdminPolls and allAdminRaisedHands; `FeaturedQuestionsSwitch` is instant with a patch. Teacher list: `AdminHighlighted` → `AdminFeatured`, no chip, star on the featured node, disabled = empty dashed node, no numbers; `SessionLinks` prop `highlighted` → `featured`; `FeaturedLabel` is dropped. `PollStateActions` gets `isFeatured` (from the route) and hides Activar outside the featured session.

Out of scope: anything not in the program design; the mail link stays as it is.

## The tasks

They live in Entire trail #3 (https://entire.com/gh/filadd/-/trails/3). Work them in this order:
1. **La marca en la base y el contrato.** Migration `0004_featured_session` with `featured`, `featured_questions` and the partial unique index. `SessionSummary` and `SessionChange` add `featured` and `featuredQuestions`; errors add `NotFeatured` (409). The changelog adds `questions-opened`, with its label, line and color.
2. **Batches que cruzan stores.** The core adds the `Write` type and the `Batch` port; `Repository` adds `writes`. `repositoryOf` builds `writes` from its `statements`, `D1Batch` implements the port, `worker.ts` wires it.
3. **Cambiar la destacada (API).** `Sessions.update` builds the leaving of the featured session as above, removes its changelog items and notifies its classroom. `SessionDisabled` and `NotFeatured` as above. Featured questions on/off create and remove `questions-opened`. `Sessions.featured` reads the mark. Tests in a new `featured.test.ts` with its own fixture.
4. **La regla de la destacada en las escrituras (API).** `featuredSession` in the student writes; Activar outside the featured session answers `NotFeatured`; the first vote stops removing `poll-opened`. The fixtures of polls, questions, raised-hands, classroom and announcements mark their featured session; the classroom without a featured session goes in its own file.
5. **Inicio del estudiante (web).** Renames, "Todas las sesiones", `railLook`, `RailNode` `later`, the star, `SessionLinks` `featured`, active polls of the featured session only, `/aula` by the mark, the `sessionSummary` fixture with the two fields.
6. **Panel de preguntas en la card (web).** `FeaturedQuestions` in the `questions` slot of `FeaturedSession`.
7. **Admin de una sesión (web).** `FeaturedSwitch`, `EnableSessionDialog`, `FeaturedEffects`, `useFeaturedSession`, `ConfirmDialog` slots, `EnabledSwitch` modal and confirmation, `useUpdateSession` without optimistic patch on waiting changes, no "Sesión N de M".
8. **Lista de sesiones del profe (web).** `AdminFeatured`, `AdminSessionRail` with `railLook`, star, dashed node for disabled, no numbers.
9. **Activar y Preguntas destacadas en el aula del profe (web).** `PollStateActions` with `isFeatured`, hiding Activar outside the featured session in the tab and the panel; `FeaturedQuestionsSwitch` above the panel's questions.

Each API test file runs on its own D1, and a D1 holds only one featured session: plan the fixtures accordingly (that is why featuring and "no featured session" get their own files).

## Lo que el diseño deja para el programa

- Dónde se arma el batch y cómo devuelve las encuestas que cierra.
- Qué error responde cada rechazo nuevo.
- Dónde vive el control de la destacada para no repetirlo en cada escritura.
- Cómo la web cuenta los efectos para las confirmaciones.
- Qué acciones del profe pierden el parche optimista.
- En qué componentes entran el panel de preguntas, el modal y las confirmaciones.
- Cómo se reparte el cálculo del camino entre el inicio y el admin.

## Decisiones de esta etapa

- **Q1 · NotFeatured**: un error nuevo, 409, para activar una encuesta o prender las preguntas destacadas fuera de la destacada. Las escrituras del estudiante no lo usan: conservan el 404 que ya devuelven para una sesión que no pueden tocar, así el estudiante no distingue una sesión vieja de una que no existe. La web no deja hacer ninguna de estas acciones fuera de la destacada, así que el rechazo solo llega con una pantalla vieja (el usuario aceptó la propuesta).
- **Q2 · El servicio arma el batch (C2)**: `Sessions.update` coordina el cambio de destacada. Pide a `SessionsStore`, `PollsStore` y `HandsStore` sus escrituras sin ejecutarlas, con `writes`, y las corre juntas con el puerto `Batch`. `writes` es la versión diferida de los métodos de escritura de `Repository`, y `repositoryOf` la arma desde las `statements` que ya tiene, así que todos los stores la heredan sin código propio. Se descartó `SessionsStore.changeFeatured`, que seguía el patrón de `MaterialsStore` (un store que escribe en tablas de otros), y un método `Write` por caso en cada store.
- **Avisos al aula**: la sesión que sale recibe `session`, `polls` y `hands`, porque el profe puede tener abierta su página en otra pestaña y las listas de su admin cambian.
- **El nodo del camino**: el inicio y el admin usan la misma regla, y por eso el cálculo vive en `rail-look.ts`. Los dos dibujan lo mismo en cada nodo: check en `done`, estrella en `live`, nada en `later`; el admin suma `locked`, vacío y punteado, para las deshabilitadas.
- **La destacada se busca una vez** (pedido del usuario): `ContentTab` la toma con `useFeaturedSession`, un `select` sobre la lista del admin, y se la pasa a los dos switches con la sesión de la página. La sesión de la página ya dice si es la destacada (`session.featured`); la lista hace falta para saber cuál es la otra.
- **Sin números en el admin** (pedido del usuario sobre el mockup de la lista): la lista del admin marca la destacada con la estrella en su nodo y no con un chip, y ningún nodo lleva número. Sin números, "Sesión N de M" deja de tener sentido: sale de la card de arriba y de la card de Contenido, y los diálogos nombran a la otra destacada por su título.
- **Q3 · Todas las sesiones**: la lista del inicio ya tiene a la destacada (prototipo), así que se titula "Todas las sesiones" con o sin destacada, como en el admin. El nodo de la destacada pierde el número y lleva una estrella, la del chip "Destacada". Los componentes del inicio y del admin toman el nombre de la marca: `FeaturedSession`, `AllSessions`, `AdminFeatured`.

# kurasu: architecture rules

verified: 2026-10-19

Answers how kurasu's backend code is split and which rules its Effect code follows.

## Knowledge

- `packages/core` defines services named after a job (sessions, polls, access, mailer) and their ports. It imports no adapter and nothing from Cloudflare, Alchemy, Drizzle or jose.
- Adapters live outside core: the D1 adapters in `packages/database`, the R2, Email Sending, JWT and Durable Object adapters in `apps/api`. The apps wire the core services to their adapters; packages never import apps.
- Expected failures are typed errors declared with Schema; the code does not catch defects as if they were expected.
- Decode everything that enters at a boundary (a request body, a stored row, a message) with its schema before using it.
- The Worker reads configuration with Effect `Config` where it is built and passes it to the layers as plain values (`Access.layer(webOrigin)`, `JoseSessionTokens(jwtSecret)`). Secrets come from varlock: `.env.schema` declares them and `.env.local`, out of git, holds them. The mail binding and the D1 resource also read two test-only variables, `KURASU_MAIL_ALLOWED_DESTINATIONS` and `KURASU_D1_IMPORT_FILES`, which `.env.schema` declares without a default, so `Config.option` reads them as absent outside the API tests.
- Declare Alchemy resources outside the Worker's runtime path, because a Worker's initialization runs once at deploy and again when the isolate starts. The API Worker builds its HTTP app, with every layer that reads D1, inside `fetch`, because the bindings exist only when the isolate starts (see `alchemy/local-dev`).
- Reads are bounded (a list has a maximum) and paginate by key, not by offset.
- D1 has no transactions: writes that must land together go in one batch.

- `app/apps/api/src/worker.ts`.
# kurasu: API shape

verified: 2026-10-19

Answers how kurasu's HTTP API is laid out: what is a route, what is a filter, and what travels inside a resource.

## Knowledge

- Each resource has one endpoint, never nested: `/api/<resource>` and `/api/<resource>/{id}`. The one exception is a resource's binary content, at `/{id}/file` (`GET /api/materials/{id}/file`).
- The student uses `/api/<resource>` and the teacher `/api/admin/<resource>`; each side gets only the operations it needs.
- The id of another resource goes in as a filter (`?sessionId=`) or in the body, never in the path.
- A resource includes the values that belong to it: the student's vote is a field of the poll (`myResponse`) and of the question (`myVote`), set with a `PATCH` on that resource.
- A list returns a summary and the detail returns the full resource (`SessionSummary` and `Session`).
- Actions that are not resources, such as requesting a login link or opening a session, stay as actions under `/api/auth/`.
- A malformed teacher request answers a typed 400 and stores nothing: `InvalidPollContent` for poll content of another type (options outside `choice`, scale labels outside `scale`) and `InvalidUpload` for a multipart upload whose fields come after the file or do not decode. Changing the access of a user id that does not exist answers `UserNotFound` (404).
- Every endpoint behind the login also answers the access middleware's errors (requesting a link and opening a session have no middleware): `Unauthenticated`, `NoAccess`, and `NotTeacher` on `/api/admin`.

allowed-tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep
---

Load mahou:basics first. Then read `.mahou/commit-changes.md` if present.

# Commit changes

Commits the changes done to this repository using conventional commits (https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/). This is the one skill whose job is committing, so the user asking for it, or a skill reaching a commit step the user approved, is the consent `basics` asks for. Pushing is not part of the job.

## Message format

```
<type>[optional scope]: <description>

[optional body]

[optional footer(s)]
```

Types:

- **fix**: patches a bug (PATCH in semantic versioning)
- **feat**: introduces a feature (MINOR)
- A `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer marks a breaking change (MAJOR) and can go on a commit of any type. Never use the `!` after the type or scope for this.
- **build**, **chore**, **ci**, **docs**, **style**, **refactor**, **perf**, **test**, with their usual meanings from `@commitlint/config-conventional`.

Footers other than `BREAKING CHANGE: <description>` follow the git trailer format.

## Procedure

1. **Analyze the repository state.** `git status` for everything modified, added and deleted; `git diff` for the nature of each change; `git diff --staged` for anything already staged. When the project has a `CLAUDE.md` or a `.mahou/commit-changes.md` that names a scope convention or a commit convention of its own, read it and follow it.

2. **Plan the groups.** Group by logical relationship: same feature, same fix, same area. Tests, type definitions and directly related changes go with the main change. Never mix unrelated changes in one commit. Refactors go in their own commit unless small and tightly coupled to the main change.

3. **Present the groups and wait.** Always, even when there is one group and it looks obvious. Show every group with its proposed message and its file list, then ask how to proceed: with one group, proceed or split further; with several, proceed or merge. Take the user's regrouping literally.

4. **Commit each approved group.** Stage only that group's files with `git add <file>...`, then commit with the agreed message. Never `git add -A` or `git add .`; an untracked file the user did not mention is not part of any group until they say so.

   A file whose changes belong to two groups is split by hunk. The file appears under both groups with a word on which change goes where. To stage one side, write the file's diff to a temporary patch with `git diff <file> > /tmp/<name>.diff`, delete the hunks that belong to the other group while keeping the diff header, and apply it with `git apply --cached /tmp/<name>.diff`. Once that group is committed, the hunks left in the working tree are what `git add <file>` stages for the other. `git add -p` is interactive and does not run here.

## Message rules

- Description in the imperative, present tense: "add", not "added" or "adding". Short, no trailing period.
- The message says **what** the change does, never why it was made or where the request came from. "fix(auth): add null check for expired tokens", never "fix: address PR comments".
- A body, when needed, is simple and direct: no file listings, no implementation walkthrough, no test section.
- **Scope** is the area of the project the change touches: the top-level module, directory, package or service name, one or two lowercase words. Check `git log` for the scopes the project already uses and reuse them. When the change spans areas, use the primary one; when nothing dominates, omit the scope.

## When something is off

- No changes: say so and stop.
- Merge conflict markers in the tree: say so and stop; nothing is committed over a conflict.
- Untracked files: ask whether they belong in a group before staging them.

El asunto no lleva el número de la sesión, que el estudiante no ve. El cuerpo lleva, en este orden, el mensaje del profe tal como lo escribió, las novedades incluidas y el link a la sesión. Sin mensaje, el cuerpo empieza por las novedades. Sin novedades, lleva el mensaje y el link. Las novedades no llevan link propio: el único link del mail es el de la sesión. Si la sesión es la destacada en el momento del envío, el link lleva a la home, donde la destacada está arriba. Si no, lleva a la home con `?sesion=<id>`, y la home despliega esa sesión en la lista y la deja en el centro de la pantalla (ver [estados de encuestas y sesiones](estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md)). El mail no saluda al estudiante por su nombre y no tiene pie, link para darse de baja ni texto legal.

> [!WARNING] El link de un mail viejo a la destacada
> La API decide si la sesión es la destacada en el momento del envío. Después de un cambio de destacada, un mail viejo con el link a la home lleva a una home con otra destacada arriba, o sin destacada, y la sesión del anuncio queda plegada en la lista. Al revés, si una sesión anunciada con `?sesion=<id>` es la destacada cuando el estudiante abre el link, el link despliega su card en la lista, y la misma sesión aparece también arriba, como destacada.

## Tasks

1. **Mark and contract.** The migration is `0004_featured_session`, with the two boolean columns and a partial unique index on `featured`.

3. **Changing the featured session.** `Sessions.update` follows the design.
   - The batch order is: unmark and turn off the leaving session, close its active polls (omitted when there are none), lower its hands, apply the change.
   - Afterwards it drops `questions-opened` and the closed polls' `poll-opened`, notifies `session`, `polls` and `hands`, and handles `questions-opened` on and off.
   - `Sessions.featured` reads the mark. A change with no leaving session uses the plain `store.update`.
4. **Write rule.** `featuredSession` replaces `visibleSession` in student writes. Activating outside the featured session answers `NotFeatured`, and the first vote keeps `poll-opened`.
5. **Student home.** `FeaturedSession`, `AllSessions`, `railLook`, the star icon, `RailNode` `later` and `SessionLinks` `featured` are in. Active polls are asked for per featured session, and `/aula` takes the mark.
6. **Questions panel.** `FeaturedQuestions` goes in the `questions` slot, and `QuestionList` takes `emptyText`.
